data.narrative:
Flapping Airplanes is a private AI & Software company founded by Benjamin Spector, Asher Spector, and Aidan Smith. The valuation and capital history remain undisclosed. The comparable universe consists of one public company (Palantir Technologies, ticker PLTR) and eight private peers including Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition.

The peer-median method, typically the primary valuation triangulation tool, is not applicable here. Despite identifying twelve same-sector peers in AI & Software, none satisfied the necessary filters for a robust comparison set: zero companies matched on stage, zero on adjacent stage, and zero on similar valuation tier. A threshold of at least three datapoints within tightly defined parameters was required to avoid the analytical error of collapsing to an all-sector median, which would introduce material noise given the heterogeneity of AI & Software valuations across different development phases and market positions.

The absence of a tight peer set and undisclosed current valuation and prior fundraising history constrain the quantitative analysis. No triangulated range can be supported without at least one methodologically sound valuation approach. Further diligence would require either (1) obtaining stage, recent valuation, and revenue or metric data for candidate peers to reassess comparability, or (2) applying alternative methods such as venture capital method or DCF analysis if financial projections are available. Current data does not permit defensible valuation synthesis.
